rationale: JOB 2's `imports` type, third measurement. The adjudicator (script/m14/tmp/scala-type-adjudicator.ts, an independent walker over the parse tree) reported `imports (file) -> treeBuilder.global.unit.global` and `-> treeBuilder.global.unit.unit` as ANALYZER-ONLY for `import treeBuilder.{global => _, unit => _}` (src/compiler/scala/reflect/quasiquotes/Parsers.scala:107). The cause is that handleImport pushed EVERY renamed segment into one module path, so two renames concatenated into `treeBuilder.global.unit`, reached three surfaces (the references target, ImportInfo.path, and the imports edges, where each selector was then appended again), and produced names no package has. Measured over the corpus: 63 clauses carry two or more renames and 103 selectors are the exclusion form `X => _`. An EXCLUSION is a name the import WITHHOLDS, so publishing it as a dependency asserts the opposite of what the statement says; the grammar spells its alias as a `wildcard` node, which is how the two forms are told apart. The single-rename form is deliberately unchanged because master-owned evidence pins it (ground-truth/scala.json + differential.ts importPathOf), and the two plain controls pin that the fix did not disturb them. The single-segment join was a second finding from the same instrument: the edge builder joined a selector onto the module path only when the path was already dotted, so the SHAPE of the import decided the precision of the edge. A third measurement from the same instrument: the dependency base is per GROUP of a Scala 3 multi-clause import, because `import sbt._, Keys._` is two dependencies and the single module path concatenates them into `sbt.Keys`. 149 multi-clause declarations on the corpus. One forbid row was RETIRED rather than fixed: `a selector list names the MEMBERS, not the bare package` stopped being assertable in this file once it also carried `import scala.collection.mutable, scala.collection.immutable`, where depending on the package IS the statement. Two rows in one fixture that contradict each other is the unassertable-expectation failure the runner warns about, and the fix is to drop the weaker one and say so.
